newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel, Motorola in phone deal.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel, Motorola in phone deal.

text.p: French telecommunications and engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom said on Thursday it had agreed a broad memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Motorola Inc on cellular telephone technology.
The agreement covers Motorola's cellular infrastructure group (CIG) and its CDMA cellular and fixed access radio systems, DECT radio systems, and mobile switching centres and transmission prducts.
The arrangement gives Alcatel access to Motorala's CDMA radio systems for cellular phones.
In parallel, Alcatel will provide Motorola with its mobile switching subsystem as well as transmission equipment.
The two companies did not disclose financial details.
CDMA stands for code division multiple access, an element of digital cellular technology which Motorola has but Alcatel lacked.

DECT, standing for Digital European Cordless Telephone, is a technology for so-called "wireless in the local loop" applications. This allows operators to offer home telecom services with wireless links to cable networks, making it unneccessary to link up all homes with cable.
DECT is a European standard and Alcatel said that with the Motorola link they hoped the standard would also catch on in the United States.
